title: Ventricular ectopic beats
summary: Premature beats that start in the ventricles, at times after every normal beat.
description: A minute of ECG in which normally conducted beats (N) alternate, at times, with premature ventricular contractions (V): early, wide and oddly shaped QRS complexes, with no P wave before them, followed by a long pause. When every other beat is ectopic the rhythm is called ventricular bigeminy (the strip at the top names the rhythm). The beats were labelled by cardiologists.
look_for: The width of a normal QRS and of an ectopic one
No P wave before an ectopic beat, and its T wave pointing the opposite way to its QRS
The pause after an ectopic beat: compare the R–R intervals before and after it

channels.name: ECG (V1)
channels.about: a chest lead, to the right of the breastbone

beats.note: Each beat was labelled by two cardiologists working independently, who then settled their differences (the reference labels of the MIT-BIH database).

legend.N: Normal beat: a normally conducted QRS (whatever the rhythm)

subject.notes: Taking Pronestyl (procainamide), as the database records; it notes that her ectopic beats all have the same shape.
